![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14224622/assets/a5a3a246f2ecb4bee6cfc46f34d14b5abc9fcf22ed0d6173ed465bfab2cfeca6.png)

Consider the finite region bounded by the curves $x=5y-2{y}^{2}$ and $x=y,$ as shown above. Find an integral expression for the volume generated when this region is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $x$-axis.
question.worked_solution:
First, let $f(y)=5y-2{y}^{2}$ and $g(y)=y.$

We start by determining the points where the curves intersect by solving the following equation for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(y) & =g(y) \\ 5y-2{y}^{2} & =y \\ 2{y}^{2}-4y & =0 \\ 2y(y-2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions are $y=0$ and $y=2.$ So, we need to integrate from $y=0$ to $y=2.$ 

Now, let's draw our usual horizontal arrow through the region to determine the left and right functions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14224622/assets/d873c0acb12392e4ea40f761c72c1903a91c4f0e9fef04b586a71697957e2401.png)

The horizontal arrow 

- *enters* the region through the left function $x=g(y)=y,$ and

- *leaves* through the right function $x=f(y)=5y-2{y}^{2}.$

Therefore, using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be expressed as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =2\pi {\int }_{c}^{d}y([\text{right}]-[\text{left}])\,\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}y([5y-2{y}^{2}]-[y])\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}y(4y-2{y}^{2})\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$
